review_results.claim_summary: Path structure (max drawdown, up/down ratio, largest move) adds predictive value beyond levels and volatility
reasons_for_accept: Genuinely new computation — existing features capture only total return, not path dynamics
Economically motivated — path quality is a real risk dimension
All data available — OHLCV bars for all universes
Low leakage risk — trailing windows only
Low implementation difficulty — standard rolling computations
No duplicate of prior work — path features were never tested in Phases 9-14
concerns: Path max_drawdown may correlate with vol_10/30 (higher vol → higher drawdown). Mitigation: include vol_10/30 in baseline feature set to measure incremental value.
Up/down ratio may be noisy at small window sizes. Mitigation: use 20-day window (16+ observations minimum).

review_results.claim_summary: Return skewness and kurtosis add predictive value as higher-order moments
reasons_for_accept: Genuinely new — all existing features are symmetric (mean, std, ratio)
Economically motivated — skewness captures tail risk, a priced risk factor in academic literature
All data available — OHLCV bars for all universes
Low leakage risk
Orthogonal to existing features by construction (different moment)
concerns: Skewness estimates are noisy with only 20 observations. Mitigation: test with 30-day window as robustness.
The sign of the skewness-return relationship is ambiguous (risk premium vs selling pressure). This is a feature, not a bug — we test both directions.

review_results.claim_summary: Macro regime (rates, inflation, unemployment) conditions stock-level prediction
reasons_for_accept: Completely new information source — no existing feature uses macro data
Economically motivated — macro conditions change how stock signals translate to returns
Data available — FRED series (DS-000003) covers CPI, DFF, UNRATE from 1947+
Low leakage risk — macro data published with known lags
Applies to all instruments uniformly — no cross-sectional leakage
concerns: Low frequency (monthly/quarterly) vs daily stock data — may be too slow for 5-day returns. Mitigation: use level and 3-month change, which capture both level and direction.
DFF is the most frequently updated (daily effective rate). UNRATE and CPI are monthly. Use last-available observation for PIT.

review_results.claim_summary: Volatility dynamics (vol-of-vol, vol change) add value beyond vol levels
reasons_for_accept: Genuinely new dimension — vol_ratio_10_30 captures level comparison, not stability
Economically motivated — vol regime transitions signal uncertainty changes
Data available — derived from existing OHLCV
Low leakage risk
concerns: Partial overlap with vol_ratio_10_30 — may not add much incremental value. This is testable.
Nested rolling computation (vol of vol) may be noisy. Mitigation: use 5-day inner window, 20-day outer window.

review_results.claim_summary: Dynamic beta and correlation add value beyond static cross-sectional ranks
reasons_for_reject: High overlap with existing market context features (mkt_ret_20, mkt_vol_20) and cross-sectional features (xs_rank_ret_20)
Beta/correlation estimates are noisy with 20-day windows — high estimation error
Market context features (Phase 12A) already tested and showed inconsistent improvement
Rolling beta requires SPY benchmark — adds dependency but existing market features already use SPY
The incremental information beyond what market context already captures is likely minimal
review_results.note: While dynamic beta is conceptually interesting, the existing market context features (FEAT-201..206) already capture market-level information. The marginal contribution of rolling beta is likely too small to justify the additional complexity and estimation noise.

summary.note: H-4 (vol dynamics) is ACCEPT for robustness testing only — it is included as a supplementary feature family but not as a primary hypothesis. H-5 (dynamic beta) is REJECTED due to high overlap with existing market context features.
